audit.whatIsWrong: Row 1 reads Skill and rows 2 and 3 read Vayne, while the packet chart gives all three to Ziggs — and whys[1], whys[2] and whys[3] on the same page say exactly that ('he zones you off every CS attempt', 'keeps chunking you', 'you still have no gap-closer').
audit.why: 49.76% over 834 games in a lane the page itself describes as poke-dominated until the first item; three rows rendered the opposite of their own explanation.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2 and 3 set to Ziggs in both layers, ratings lowered to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why said to force fights 'on Satchel Charge's cooldown' without saying why that matters, and the early stage explanations named no ranges at all.
audit.why: Satchel Charge is his only escape — Riot's text gives it a self-knockback and no other mobility exists in the kit — so its 20/18/16/14/12s cooldown is the entire first-item window.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why now states that it is his only escape; phases[1..3].why carry the real ranges and cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d had no numbers; Hexplosive Minefield appears nowhere on the page, Satchel Charge's recast detonation is never stated, and Short Fuse's empowered auto is never mentioned.
audit.why: Bouncing Bomb is 850 range on 6s down to 4s; Satchel Charge reaches 1000 and 'detonates after a delay, or when this ability is activated again', so the recast is the thing to step away from; Hexplosive Minefield lays a 900-range slowing minefield on 16s that denies the approach a Vayne with no dash depends on; Short Fuse periodically arms an empowered auto whose cooldown drops each time he casts.
audit.corrected: All four rewritten with the numbers, the recast rule and the Short Fuse tell; the minefield added to phases[2].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge was tracked as the key cooldown with no duration attached.
audit.why: 20s at rank 1 dropping to 12s is the window the whole first-item plan hangs on.

edits.before: Q tumble resets make your spacing untouchable. Only take the trade when Ziggs's Satchel Charge is down.
edits.after: Bouncing Bomb is 850 range on 6s and you have no dash — give the wave and last-hit from behind minions.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Ziggs must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: His max-range poke chunks you as you try to stack Silver Bolts, and Hexplosive Minefield slows every approach you have.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Satchel Charge's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Still his: Bouncing Bomb drops to 4.5s at rank 4 and Satchel Charge knocks you out of your own range from 1000. Farm under tower.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Satchel Charge's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — close the moment Satchel Charge is spent, since it is his only escape.

edits.before: His knockback + self-peel escape. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 and it is his only escape — close the gap inside that window.

edits.before: Ziggs wastes Satchel Charge — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Silver Bolts needs three consecutive hits — do not break off at two.

edits.before: That is Ziggs's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: It detonates on a delay or on recast — step out before the second press.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Short Fuse arms an empowered auto — the wind-up is his tell.

notes: Satchel Charge carries a 'percentHealth' derived flag and the missing-interactions rule 'resistances-invalidated', but Riot's own W text describes plain magic damage plus a knockback with no percent-health component. Per the contradiction rule I trusted the description and wrote no claim that armour or MR is invalidated here — flagging the flag as a likely tooltip-parsing misfire.
